taxonomic_note: Current project treatment follows Flora of North America for Cissus trifoliata; Cissus incisa is retained as a familiar synonym.
look_here_first: Start with the thick 3-parted to trifoliolate leaves and stout reddish stems, then confirm the unbranched tendrils and dark berry clusters.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Later manual Deep Review locked Travis, Bexar, and Comal as exact project target-zone occurrences and cross-checked the species against BONAP/NAPA.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not infer counties from Edwards Plateau/Blackland Prairie mapping alone; the PASS uses exact county evidence.

best_field_traits: leaflets thick to slightly succulent with coarse irregular teeth
fleshy red to red-brown stems with swollen or warty nodes
berries blue-black to black when mature
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Separate from Parthenocissus by the usual 3-parted/trifoliolate fleshy foliage rather than palmately 5–7-foliolate leaves; separate from Vitis with the thick 3-parted leaves, stem/node texture, tendrils, and reproductive details rather than berries alone.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Use the thick 3-parted foliage, swollen/warty reddish nodes, unbranched tendrils, and dark berries together; grape-like fruit alone is not diagnostic.
